content.text:
I've submitted **index 23** (Ca 0.14, Co 0.70, Mn 0.16) as the best composition. It gave 3×10⁻⁸ A, the only positive photocurrent I found. That signal is very weak, so I don't know how close it is to the library's actual best.

I had only 3 merit measurements, so I measured points in three different regions of the library:

| Index | Composition (Ca/Co/Mn) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 110 | 0.15 / 0.21 / 0.64 (Mn-rich) | 0 A |
| 23 | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 (Co-rich) | **3×10⁻⁸ A** |
| 10 | 0.53 / 0.32 / 0.15 (Ca-rich) | −5×10⁻⁸ A (negative current, so not working as a photoanode) |

**Limitations:**
- **Spending the last measurement on the Ca-rich region didn't pay off.** The Gaussian-process model suggested staying near index 23 (it proposed index 24), but I tried the unexplored Ca-rich region instead. It came back negative.
- **I used none of the 5 XRD measurements**, so no crystal phase was confirmed for any film.
- **I couldn't read the full phase list**, because it was too large to return. The materials-model checks I made before each measurement were therefore only loosely tied to the compositions:
  - MACE puts the Co₃O₄ spinel on the stability hull.
  - MEGNet predicts a band gap of about 0 eV for Co₃O₄.
  - MEGNet gives about 0.9 eV (HSE) or about 0 eV (PBE) for a Mn oxide. I'm assuming mp-18759 is that Mn oxide; I didn't confirm its formula.
